_README: CRM's PUBLISHED Best-of-N accuracies, transcribed by hand. Nothing here is measured by
this repo and nothing here may be recomputed by it -- that is the entire point: these are
the paper's numbers, ours come out of scripts/eval_bon.sh, and scripts/report_bon.py puts
FILL THIS IN before quoting any comparison. Every value below is null, and report_bon.py
prints our column alone (with a warning) until they are real numbers.
Units: PERCENT, 0-100, matching what crm_grader returns (eval_utils.py multiplies by 100).
If the paper reports fractions, convert here, not in the report script.
Keys under each file are METHOD NAMES exactly as the paper labels them. Add or remove
rows freely -- report_bon.py renders whatever is here. Keep 'CRM' if the paper's own
method is in the table; that is the row the comparison is actually about.
'baseline_first_candidate' is the no-reward-model number (accuracy of the first sampled
response). IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ENTRY IN THIS FILE. It does not depend on any reward
model, so if the paper reports it and our harness does not reproduce it to within sampling
noise, the candidate pool or the grader differ and NOTHING else in the table is comparable.
Fill it in even if you fill in nothing else.
